r: I wasn't able to find any clues surrounding the grave site. Is there something you're not telling me?

mg_lie_to_vaelric_20.m: No, just a suspicion I had. In any event, thanks for looking into it for me. Good luck on your search for Andor.

mg_vaelric_buy_insectbance_10.m: I'll take all of the ingredients and your {4800} gold now and I will mix you up a batch of ten tonics

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_10.m: So, it is done? You struck him down, ended his torment by force?

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_15.m: He exhales sharply, shaking his head.

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_20.m: I suppose I should have expected as much.

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_30.m: His gaze lingers on you, his expression hard to read. Somewhere between frustration and resignation.

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_40.m: And what of the hauntings? Is it over?

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_50.m: With your hesitation preventing you from getting a word in...

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_60.m: I see. You took the ring for yourself and left his spirit unfulfilled. That was your choice.

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_70.m: He lets out a slow breath, his voice quieter now, laced with disappointment.

mg_vaelric_defeated_eryndor_90.m: [Turning away, he mutters:] I will take what peace I can, while it lasts. But do not expect my gratitude.

mg_vaelric_other_potions_10.m: I also have other potions for sale. Would you like to take a look?

mg_vaelric_reward_10.m: You did it? You were able to help me? You have prevented the future hauntings?
r: Yes. Hence my being here with my hand out.

mg_vaelric_reward_20.m: Well, let me start by saying that you have done me a great service, and for that, I will offer you something few others could. I am no merchant, but I do have remedies, ones you will not find elsewhere. One in particular may prove invaluable to you: the Insectbane tonic.

mg_vaelric_reward_30.m: This tonic does more than ease a fever or numb the pain of a bite. It eliminates the infection entirely. If you have already fallen victim to the Insect contagion poison, one dose will purge it from your body. But more than that, it grants temporary immunity against reinfection. For a time, no swamp vermin, no festering bite, no tainted sting will take hold of you.

mg_vaelric_reward_40.m:
But such a remedy does not come cheaply. If you wish for me to prepare this tonic, you must gather the necessary ingredients yourself. Here is what I require:

Five Duskbloom flowers. These rare blossoms can be found in the deepest parts of the swamp, but the creatures there tend to be attracted to them. Their properties are delicate, so bring them fresh.

Five Mosquito proboscises. Harvested from the swamp mosquitoes. You will find no shortage of these creatures near stagnant waters, but mind their bites.

Ten bottles of swamp water. You will find plenty just outside my home. Surface water won't do. You'll need to reach deep, past the filth floating on top. The best stuff is settled at the bottom. Dark, thick, and rich with what gives the swamp its potency. Fill the bottles with that. Take these empty bottles and fill them yourself.

One sample of Mudfiend goo. A secretion found in the depths of mines and tunnels along the Duleian Road. It is the key component that binds the other ingredients together.

mg_vaelric_reward_45.m:
I require:
Five Duskbloom flowers. These rare blossoms can be found in the deepest parts of the swamp, but the creatures there tend to be attracted to them. Their properties are delicate, so bring them fresh.

Five Mosquito proboscises. Harvested from the swamp mosquitoes. You will find no shortage of these creatures near stagnant waters, but mind their bites.

Dark, thick, and rich with what gives the swamp its potency. Fill the bottles with that. Take these empty bottles and fill them yourself.

mg_vaelric_reward_50.m: Bring me these, and I shall prepare ten vials of the tonic for you. But understand this: my craft is no charity. If you seek to replenish your supply, you must pay the price. Four hundred and eighty gold per vial. A steep price, perhaps, but a fair one for something that could mean the difference between life and death.

mg_vaelric_reward_60.m: I'll take all of the ingredients and your {4800} gold now and I will mix you up a batch of ten tonics

mg_vaelric_reward_70.m: Here you go, ten Insectbane tonics.

mg_vaelric_reward_Not_enough_gold.m: You see, I have to make ten tonics at a time and because I refuse to waste any of them, you must buy all ten at a cost of {4800} gold. Do you have the gold?

mg_vaelric_reward_missing_ing_10.m: You don't have what I require in order to make them.

mg_vaelric_reward_missing_ing_20.m:
No, you don't. I already told you, if you wish for me to prepare this tonic, you must gather the necessary ingredients yourself. Here is what I require:

mg_vaelric_story_10.m: Vaelric's expression darkens, his fingers tightening around his staff. He turns away for a moment, exhaling slowly before speaking.
r: He says you treated him once, but you buried him alive. That's why he haunts you. He wants his ring back, or the hauntings will continue.
Please tell me more about Eryndor.

mg_vaelric_story_20.m: Eryndor... Yes, I remember. He came to me alone, desperate, barely able to stand. His condition was severe, far beyond anything my tinctures and poultices could mend. I did everything I knew. I bled out the sickness, cooled his fever, forced broth past his lips. But it wasn't enough. One morning, I found him still as death. No breath, no warmth. His skin had gone pale and lifeless.

mg_vaelric_story_30.m: He rubs his temple, his voice quieter now.

mg_vaelric_story_40.m: I had no choice but to lay him to rest. There was no kin to claim him, no priest to see to his rites. So I carried him to the graveyard myself, dug the earth with my own hands, and gave him what peace I could. It was the right thing to do... or so I thought.

mg_vaelric_story_50.m: His jaw tightens, regret flashing in his eyes.

mg_vaelric_story_60.m: But I was wrong. I was wrong. Somehow, he still lived. I don't know if it was some illness that mimicked death or if I simply failed to see the life still in him. Either way, my hands put him in that grave, and now his suffering is on me.

mg_vaelric_story_70.m: He hesitates, then steps toward a cabinet, opening a drawer with a sigh.

mg_vaelric_story_80.m: If his spirit will rest with this ring, take it. If that will end this curse, then let it be done.

vaelric_alone_10.m: Step lightly, wanderer. The swamp doesn't take kindly to just anyone, and neither do I. Why are you before me?
r: Why are you living out here alone?

vaelric_alone_25.m: Once, I was a celebrated healer. They called me a miracle worker for curing the incurable. My methods were...unconventional. Leeches, parasitic creatures, even plants most would call poisonous. I used whatever the swamp could offer.

vaelric_alone_28.m: Innovation often breeds fear. When a Laumwill noble entrusted me with his life, I used every method I knew to save him. But he died under my care, and the courts called it murder. The Laumwills made certain there was no place for me among civilized men.

vaelric_alone_30.m: You ask for much considering you are someone who has given me nothing in return. If you want my aid, you'll need to earn it. A creature stalks my property, not an ordinary beast but one corrupted by the same darkness that haunts this land. Deal with it, and we'll talk.

vaelric_alone_40.m: A swamp creature, but far from the kind you'd expect to see. This one is massive, venomous, and ravenous. It's draining the life from my medicinal pools. Strength alone won't save you. You'll need to learn the ways of the swamp.

vaelric_andor_10.m: Step lightly, wanderer. The swamp doesn't take kindly to strangers, and neither do I. What brings you to my domain?
r: I'm searching for someone, my brother, Andor. He looks like...

vaelric_andor_20.m: Ah, the one with fire in his eyes and fear in his heart. He came here seeking knowledge, though knowledge often demands a price. Are you here to pay it as well?
r: What did he want from you?

vaelric_andor_30.m: What every ambitious fool wants: power and mastery over forces that should be left alone. Your brother was in a hurry when he left, clutching what he came for. You might ask yourself why.
r: Why are you living out here alone?

vaelric_creature_killed_10.m: You've proven resourceful. Perhaps you are worthy of the knowledge I carry. The swamp holds more than muck and mire, and so do the creatures that call it home.
r: You mentioned leeches earlier. What did you mean by that?

vaelric_creature_killed_20.m: Leeches are simple creatures, but they hold incredible power. With the right knowledge, they can purge poison, stop bleeding, and heal wounds that no salve can touch. Few have the courage to learn their secrets.

vaelric_creature_killed_30.m: I don't waste my time on fools, but you've proven yourself. Watch closely.

vaelric_creature_killed_40.m: See how the leech attaches itself? It draws out the bad humors, cleansing the blood. Placement is everything. Here, take this.
r: [Extend my hand and take the leech.]
[Extend my hand and take the leech.]

vaelric_creature_killed_5.m: Have you killed the creature that threatens my way of life?
r: Yes, and here, I have this thing that proves it. [shows the 'Corrupted swamp core' to Vaelric]
Yes, but I can't prove it. I will return with proof.

vaelric_creature_killed_50.m: Don't underestimate them. In skilled hands, they are as effective as any blade or potion. Use them wisely.
r: Thank you. Is there anything else I should know?

vaelric_creature_killed_60.m: Yes. Don't waste them on minor cuts or trifling ailments. Save them for when they're truly needed. The swamp still has more to teach you, if you are willing to learn.

vaelric_creature_killed_70.m: By the way, I'll take that 'Corrupted swamp core' now.
r: Oh, yeah, sure. I don't need that thing.

vaelric_creature_killed_narrator.m: Vaelric produces a jar filled with wriggling leeches and demonstrates their use on a wounded arm.

r: You mentioned leeches earlier. What did you mean by that?

vaelric_graveyard_10.m: Oh, those people? They are nobody.
r: Really? "Nobody" you say? Nobody is a "nobody".

vaelric_graveyard_20.m: Well, one or two of them may have been those that sought my aid and it was too late for them. The others? Most likely unfortunate Galmore miners who lost their lives under false promises of riches.
r: I see. Thank you for explaining this.
I noticed that one of the graves looks to have been dug-up in the not-so-distant past.
The northwest one near the river.

vaelric_met.m: So, you've returned. Tell me, do the leeches whisper their secrets to you yet? Or are you still grasping at the edges of what this swamp has to offer?
r: You stated that if I helped you kill that venomous creature that you would tell more about Andor.
That graveyard, the one directly south of here, who were those people?
Actually, I am here to give you an update on that graveyard exploration you sent me on.
I spoke to a ghost in the Galmore encampment. His name is Eryndor...
No, that's old news. Try and keep up, won't you? I'm here to collect my reward?
No, that's old news. Try and keep up, won't you? I'm here to inform you that I've defeted Eryndor's spirit.
What do I need to give you in order for you to make those Insectbane tonics? I want some now.
Can we talk about the Insectbane tonic?
I would like to see your other potions for sale.

vaelric_met_10.m: No, no, no. I said "if you want my aid, you'll need to earn it", and indeed you did receive my aid as I taught you about the leeches.

vaelric_need_to_kill_creature_10.m: Why are you still here? Go kill that massive, venomous, and ravenous creature for me, then we will talk!

vaelric_restless_grave_10.m: Vaelric pauses, his expression tense as if piecing something together.

vaelric_restless_grave_11.m: That's... unsettling. If what you say is true, we need to understand what happened there. Something doesn't sit right with this. Please go back to the graveyard and search for clues.
r: No, I don't think so. Not this time. I'm tired of helping the pathetic with their problems.
OK, but this better be worth my time.
Actually, I found some clues already.
I found this bell in the graveyard. [Show Vaelric]
I found this music box in the graveyard. [Show Vaelric]

vaelric_restless_grave_15.m: Look for anything that might tell us more about who was buried there and why the grave was disturbed.

vaelric_restless_grave_found_clue_10.m: Interesting, but not helpful. Go back and search for something useful. It makes sense if you search close by to where you found this other item. And don't keep running back to me every time you find something so mundane.

r: I found this broken bell and a music box. [Show Vaelric.]

vaelric_restless_grave_found_clues_20.m: I see. Interesting, but not very helpful. Go explore the Galmore encampment east of the graveyard and report back to me when you find something helpful.

mg_restless_grave.40: I discovered a music box in the graveyard. It was partially buried and obscured by overgrown grass.
mg_restless_grave.45: I discovered the skeletal remains of a human beneath a covering of grass and weeds. I wonder if it's related to why that grave plot is dug up?

mg_restless_grave.63: Vaelric has told me his side of the story. He claimed that Eryndor came to him desperate, in a severe condition and Vaeltic said he did everything he could to save Eryndor's life. Thinking that Eryndor was dead, Vaelric buried him.
mg_restless_grave.65: After hearing Eryndor's story, I decided that he has been wronged. I also agreed to get his ring back from Vaelric.

mg_restless_grave.110: When I refused to return the ring, Eryndor attacked me.
mg_restless_grave.111: I defeated Eryndor and prevented the hauntings of Vaelric...for now, but I feel that they will resume someday.
mg_restless_grave.115: Vaelric is now able to mix up some Insectbane tonic for me.
mg_restless_grave.120: I've informed Vaelric that I defeated Eryndor but was not able to promise an end to the hauntings, Vaelric was dissatisfied with me and the outcome even going as far as saying that Andor is a better person than I am.
mg_restless_grave.123: Eryndor has asked me to find Celdar, a woman from Sullengard and give her the mysterious music box because he has no need for it and it's the right thing to do. swamp_healer.10: I encountered Vaelric, a reclusive healer living in the swamp between Mt. Galmore and Stoutford. He refused to help me unless I dealt with a dangerous creature corrupting his medicinal pools.
swamp_healer.20: I defeated the monstrous creature that I found on Vaelric's land. This creature was enormous and venomous, feeding on the lifeblood of the swamp.
swamp_healer.30: Vaelric rewarded me for my efforts by teaching me how to use leeches to heal bleeding wounds. He warned me to save them for dire situations and respect their power.

andor.1: My father Mikhail says that Andor has not been home since yesterday. I should go look for him in the village.
andor.10: Leonid tells me that he saw Andor talking to Gruil. I should go ask Gruil if he knows more.
andor.20: Gruil wants me to bring him a poison gland. Then he might talk more. He tells me that some poisonous snakes have such a gland.
andor.30: Gruil tells me that Andor was looking for someone called Umar. I should go ask his friend Gaela in Fallhaven to the east.
andor.40: I talked to Gaela in Fallhaven. He tells me to go see Bucus and ask about the Thieves' Guild.
andor.50: Bucus has allowed me to enter the hatch in the derelict house in Fallhaven. I should go talk to Umar.
andor.51: Umar in the Fallhaven Thieves' Guild recognized me, but must have me confused with Andor. Apparently, Andor has been to see him.
andor.55: Umar told me that Andor went to see a potion maker called Lodar. I should search for his hideaway.
andor.61: I heard a story in Loneford, where it seemed like Andor had been in Loneford, and that he might have had something to do with the illness that the people are suffering from there. I am not sure if it actually was Andor. If it was Andor, why would he have made the people of Loneford ill?
andor.62: Andor might have gone to do some business with a rich man in Brimhaven after he left Loneford.
andor.65: It looks like Andor was involved in the destruction of the Brimhaven dam.
andor.70: I have found the potion-maker Lodar, and heard his story about Andor. Andor went to visit Lodar in his hideaway to get a sample of something called Narwood extract. Lodar happened to notice that there was someone travelling together with Andor, that hid among the trees and did not seem to want Lodar to spot him.
andor.71: Shortly after Andor and the person he was travelling with had left, strange things started to happen in the woods around Lodar's hideaway, and Lodar himself seemed to be affected by it somehow. Lodar believes that something disturbed the tomb below his cabin, and awoke the Hira'zinn.
andor.72: Since I helped Lodar defeat the Hira'zinn, he promised to help me in return. He gave me a piece of paper that should allow me to enter the Valanyr temple of the Shadow in Nor City. He told me to seek out lady Lydalon in the temple for further assistance.
andor.80: All clues so far as to where Andor went point to Nor City. I should travel to Nor City by following the Duleian road to the southeast and look for more clues there.
andor.85: Andor may have been in Stoutford.
andor.86: Andor had something to do with the demon under the church in Stoutford.
andor.90: At Castle Guynmart I learned from Steward Unkorh that some time ago Andor was also there as a guest.
andor.92: Unkorh gave me the bonemeal potion box that Andor had given him for safekeeping.
andor.100: While exploring the town of Sullengard, I so happened to stumble upon my mother and my aunt to whom I have never met. Mother has insisted that I go home so we can talk.
andor.110: After talking with mother back at home, she and I tried to brainstorm about where Andor could be. She reminded me about Andor's friend Stanwick who lives in Brightport. We agreed that going to talk to him might be the next logical thing to do.
andor.120: In the dungeons of Laeroth manor, Kotheses, the torturer, mentioned that he had taught Andor the basics of torturing.
andor.125: Vaelric confirmed that Andor visited him recently. Andor sought to learn Vaelric's skills and left quickly, clutching what he came for. His actions raise more questions about his intentions.
andor.126: In Brightport, I was finally able to meet Stanwick, but due to his hazy memory, he was not able to help me learn anything about the whereabouts of Andor.
andor.127: Regaining his peace of mind after I helped him, Stanwick said he'll tell me more about Andor, once he gathers his thoughts.
andor.128: Stanwick gave me a signet ring that I should show to his father. Jorwick, in Nor City.
andor.130: Andor was trying to find out from Seraphina about terrible monsters in the hideout near the place with the larval burrowers.
andor.131: Elysa in the Brightport's thieves guild told me that Andor has bought a map to the sewers of Feygard.
andor.132: While investigating the Brightport theft I learned from Bryma that Andor was the one who stole the important document, and brought it to her in exchange for her alchemy knowledge.
andor.140: I saw Andor in the mountains of Galmore. We were able to exchange a few words before he disappeared again.
andor.145: I met Andor on the road to Feygard, where he was buying food from Rosmara. He disappeared again.
andor.147: I met Andor on the road to Nor City, where he was buying supplies from Alynndir. He disappeared again.
andor.910: I decided to settle down on the top of Mt. Galmore. For this I needed to find a rich and discreet man to rebuild the ruins according to my wishes. Andor will now have to go and find himself.
andor.912: The construction contract for my new home was completed. I was curious to see what it would look like.
andor.914: I visited my new residence on the top of Mt. Galmore. There I would help the people of Dhayavar as a hero and protect them from villains. Or would I become a villain myself? We'll see.
andor.999: [Quest is not completable at this time.]
